facts.text: Bloubergstrand owes its name to a nearby hill that turns blue from ships approaching Table Bay, originally called Blaauwberg by the Dutch.
The Battle of Blaauwberg, fought in 1806, was South Africa's first major military skirmish and marked the start of British control.
Bloubergstrand’s beach is famed for its classic view of Table Mountain across Table Bay and ranks among the world’s top kitesurfing spots.
Robben Island lies just 6.9 kilometres west of Bloubergstrand’s coast, a short boat ride away for history buffs.
During Apartheid, Bloubergstrand was a whites‑only beach and suburb; the ban was lifted in 1991 after the Group Areas Act ended.
Ons Huisie, now a Provincial Heritage Site, has a colourful history tied to Bloubergstrand’s early development and still serves as a cultural landmark.
